item.title: Optimizing Comet Implementation: Why Apache/PHP Threads Struggle with Long Polling
item.description:
“Optimizing Comet Implementation: Why Apache/PHP Threads Struggle with Long Polling”

How can we effectively implement Comet-style, long-lived connections, particularly when constrained by traditional server models like Apache with PHP? The inherent design of certain web server modules and scripting environments presents significant scaling hurdles for persistent HTTP requests.

The Apache Worker Thread Dilemma

When employing Apache with standard request handling, each incoming request, especially long-polling or COMET requests that intentionally delay completion, consumes a dedicated worker thread until that request resolves. This persistent holding of threads directly impacts scalability.
